phases.title: Phase 1: Extract outer API layer (1 module)
phases.strategy: Place API Gateway in front. Route new requests to extracted microservice; legacy endpoints stay live until traffic shifts.
phases.rollback: Switch API Gateway route back to legacy endpoints
phases.rationale: Controllers are the outermost layer — they hold routing and input validation but no persistent state. Extracting them first lets us place a gateway over the legacy monolith and start splitting traffic. Scope: 1 module(s), 599 LOC, 4 known vulnerabilities.

phases.title: Phase 2: Extract shared domain models (1 module)
phases.strategy: Extract domain entities into a shared contracts package consumed by both the legacy app and the new service.
phases.rollback: Revert contracts package version; legacy model remains authoritative
phases.rationale: Domain models are the contracts between caller and callee. Lifting them into a shared package unblocks parallel work on the dependent services. Scope: 1 module(s), 324 LOC, 0 known vulnerabilities.

phases.title: Phase 3: Extract data access layer (1 module)
phases.strategy: Introduce an anti-corruption layer over the legacy DB. New service reads via views; writes flow through the legacy path until the schema is owned by the new service.
phases.rollback: Remove anti-corruption layer; reads/writes resume on legacy schema
phases.rationale: Data access is high risk because schema changes require coordination with every consumer. We use an anti-corruption layer to decouple the new service from legacy SQL. Scope: 1 module(s), 643 LOC, 10 known vulnerabilities.

phases.title: Phase 4: Audit and reclassify (1 module)
phases.strategy: Audit the module before extraction. If it matches the shared library pattern, treat it as high risk and handle it near the end of the plan.
phases.rollback: Document the fall-back procedure before starting this phase
phases.rationale: These modules could not be classified automatically. Audit them before starting extraction to determine the correct strangler strategy. Scope: 1 module(s), 1,330 LOC, 0 known vulnerabilities.

phases.title: Phase 5: Untangle shared legacy libraries (1 module)
phases.strategy: Identify consumers and lift the shared module into a versioned package. Extract one consumer at a time; deprecate the shared copy once all consumers migrate.
phases.rollback: Restore shared library import; republish legacy version
phases.rationale: Shared libraries are the hardest to extract — every consumer is affected. We handle them after leaf modules are stable so we can migrate consumers one at a time. Scope: 1 module(s), 2,877 LOC, 127 known vulnerabilities.

narrative: **Pre-assigned decision: REFACTOR** (phase Q3). Rationale: Mature app with well-understood domain and the highest documentation coverage in the portfolio. Refactor rather than replace. Priority focus: credentials centralization, FK restoration, stored procedure modernization, cyclomatic complexity reduction. The app-01 application contains 6 modules (5,808 lines of code, 141 known vulnerabilities). NexusForge proposes a 5-phase strangler decomposition covering controller, model, repository, shared, unknown. Total estimated effort: 23 engineer-days (~4 working weeks for a single engineer, or ~1 weeks for a 4-engineer team working in parallel). Each phase is independently deployable and reversible — no big-bang cut-over.
